VibePascal v54 -- arm-linux CROSS compiler -- runs on x86_64-linux, emits 32-bit arm-linux
Source commit: b7d2d9676ecf1d7d8250cd460b9c48069920513e
Compiler fix:  b9cb8fea875670cfc48f7d83b88d4af39a28aa6e
Parent release: v53 (9e20efe4d6912fe6a9558c442ae4fa8d5dfe3045)
Built: 2026-09-10 on x86_64-linux
Binary: bin/ppcrossarm  md5 0138dae1259db05136d6fa7391a2a213

ABI: ARMHF -- ARM EABI5, HARD float (VFP).  This is the ABI of Raspberry Pi OS
32-bit and of Debian/Ubuntu armhf.  It is NOT compatible with an armel
(soft-float) system.  The compiler reports "Target OS: Linux for ARMHF".
An armel build is possible from the same source (the tree's own default is in
fact armel, compiler/fpcdefs.inc:249), but this host has only armhf cross
binutils, so armhf is what was built and verified.  Ask FPCDeveloper if you
need the armel pair.

UNITS ARE INCLUDED SEPARATELY and are REQUIRED.  arm-linux is a NEW platform for
this fork -- unlike win64/aarch64/i386 there is no pre-existing unit set to
reuse, so pair this binary with
  vibepascal-v54-arm-linux-units.tar.gz
and point the compiler at it (-Fu<prefix>/units/arm-linux, or an fpc.cfg).

Change (same as the rest of v54): an untyped INTEGER initialiser for an inline
var (and for an inferred `for var i := ...` counter) now infers NativeInt
instead of the hard-coded LongInt.  On a 32-bit target such as this one
NativeInt is 4 bytes -- and is the same type as LongInt -- so the visible effect
of that half is simply that the width follows the target.  A string or char
literal initialiser now infers exactly what a bare `string` denotes at that
point; under -Mdelphiunicode/-Munleashed that is the wide string.

VERIFIED (on the build host, x86_64-linux):
  - The compiler and the full arm-linux RTL (99 units) build clean from the
    v54 source commit, exit 0.
  - tests/test/tinlinevarnativeint1.pp -- the 45-assertion v54 matrix -- COMPILES
    and LINKS for arm-linux, producing a real ELF 32-bit ARM EABI5 executable.
  - Compile-time self-check: SizeOf(NativeInt)=4 and SizeOf(Pointer)=4 on this
    target ($if/$fatal probe, so a wrong width would fail the build).
  - String inference proven with a working negative control: `var s := 'hello'`
    under -Munleashed binds to a `var UnicodeString` parameter, and the same
    probe against `var AnsiString` is REJECTED with
    'Call by var for arg no. 1 has to match exactly: Got "UnicodeString"'.
    So the inferred type really is the wide string, not merely assignable to it.
  - NOT a discriminator, stated plainly: on 32-bit ARM NativeInt and LongInt are
    the same type, so a var-parameter probe cannot tell the v54 rule from the
    old one.  (Superseded below: the 32-bit half is now proven by execution on
    a 32-bit ARM target itself, under qemu-user, not only on i386-linux.)

RUNTIME: this cross compiler WAS EXECUTED on the build host -- it is what built
the 99-unit arm-linux RTL and every arm executable listed above, so its own
runtime behaviour is directly demonstrated.

UPDATE 2026-09-10 -- the ARM executables it emits now RUN too, correcting the
original text here.  That text claimed "this host has no qemu"; qemu-user-static
was simply not installed, and it is a stock Ubuntu package one command away.
With it, the arm output of this cross compiler executes: the 45-assertion v54
matrix reports checks=45 fails=0, NativeInt=4, VERDICT:PASS, exit 0, and the
330-line cy1096 block-scope finalization matrix reports MATRIX PASS with every
corner released exactly once.  See dist/arm-linux/VERSION.txt for the full
evidence list and for the limits of emulation -- qemu-user is not a Raspberry
Pi, and nobody has run these artifacts on physical ARM hardware yet.
